answer: Sequential work anchoring: each agent must complete a verified micro-task chain (e.g., labeling, transcription) before its outputs count. An atlas of task histories records provenance per identity. A willow rule ties voting weight to accumulated verified completions, not holdings. New identities start at zero and must redo the chain; forging N identities costs N times the labor hours, which cannot be bought or transferred. Collusion only shifts work, not its cost.
